title: Follow one piece of data
subtitle: Separate browser, server, API and storage roles.
concept: Trace input, processing, persistence and display to locate failures and decide whether a server is needed.
intuition: Track a parcel through dispatch, transport and delivery to find where progress stopped.
objectives: Describe an action's input, processing, saving and display stages.
Explain whether shared data is required before introducing server-side services.

body.title: Trace this example first
body.text: The input supplies text; app.mjs handles submission; tasks.mjs validates and produces a new list; app.mjs writes localStorage and renders it. Plans are not sent to a server. The local server only delivers HTML, CSS and JavaScript. A server.mjs file does not imply a cloud database.

body.title: Give each term a purpose
body.text: The frontend presents and interacts in the browser. A backend commonly manages shared data, permissions or business rules on a server. An API defines communication, such as fields sent to /tasks and returned results. A database organizes stored data. Small projects do not automatically need all of them.

body.title: Let requirements determine structure
body.text: A personal single-browser list can use local storage. Two devices sharing data need accessible shared storage and an identity/permission design. Publishing static files shares the program, not your browser's records. Decide data location and access before implementation.

formalDefinition.text: Trace input, processing, persistence and display to locate failures and decide whether a server is needed.
conditions: For small personal learning projects. In shared repositories, follow the team's conventions.

workedExamples.title: Locate persistence failure
workedExamples.problem: An item appears but disappears on refresh. Where first?
steps: Creation and rendering have visible results.
Check storage errors and the key used.
Confirm protocol, host and port are unchanged after refresh.
workedExamples.answer: Inspect saving and loading first. localStorage is origin-specific: http://127.0.0.1:5180 and another port use separate storage. Do not rewrite the entire interface first.

workedExamples.title: Explain a public URL
workedExamples.problem: After static publication, will classmates see my list?
steps: Separate program files from user data.
Records stay in your browser's origin-specific storage.
There are no accounts or shared data services.
workedExamples.answer: Classmates receive the same program but use their own browser storage. Static publication does not upload your list or migrate it to a new origin.

commonMistakes.claim: A server file implies backend business logic.
commonMistakes.correction: Here the server only serves static files; it does not handle list records.

commonMistakes.claim: Publishing a page synchronizes every device.
commonMistakes.correction: A shared URL and shared user data are separate. Synchronization needs its own design.

practice.problem: What stages does this example's data pass through?
practice.answer: Input → app.mjs event → tasks.mjs rules → localStorage → rendered page.
solution: A saving failure needs feedback, not a claim of success.

practice.problem: Which requirements change the local-storage design?
practice.answer: Synchronization, multiuser sharing or permissions require a shared-data and identity design.
solution: Renaming localStorage does not implement synchronization.

practice.problem: The mobile page works but lacks old records. Is this necessarily a bug?
practice.answer: No. Local storage is device-specific. If synchronization is required, the design is insufficient.

practice.problem: Receiving API data does not mean what?
practice.answer: It does not prove the page displays correctly or that client input can be trusted.
solution: Separate interface contracts, processing and presentation.

learningCheck.question: Does static publishing automatically upload the browser's list?
choices: No; a separate data design is needed
feedback: Static-file publishing does not read your records.
Program files and user data are distinct.
Changing ports instead changes the storage origin.

choices: Keep the original scope but declare completion
